Regression in 5.2.3: pytest tries to collect random __init__.py files
This was caught by our build server this morning.  It seems that pytest 5.2.3 tries to import any `__init__.py` file under the current directory. (We have some package that is only used on windows and cannot be imported on linux.)

Here is a minimal example using tox that reproduces the problem (I'm running on Debian 10 with Python 3.7.3):
```sh
❯❯❯ mkdir foobar
❯❯❯ echo 'assert False' >! foobar/__init__.py
❯❯❯ cat > tox.ini <<EOF
[tox]
envlist = py37-pytest{522,523}
skipsdist = true

[testenv]
deps =
    pytest522: pytest==5.2.2
    pytest523: pytest==5.2.3
commands = pytest
EOF
❯❯❯ tox
py37-pytest522 installed: atomicwrites==1.3.0,attrs==19.3.0,importlib-metadata==0.23,more-itertools==7.2.0,packaging==19.2,pkg-resources==0.0.0,pluggy==0.13.0,py==1.8.0,pyparsing==2.4.5,pytest==5.2.2,six==1.13.0,wcwidth==0.1.7,zipp==0.6.0

diff --git a/src/_pytest/python.py b/src/_pytest/python.py
--- a/src/_pytest/python.py
+++ b/src/_pytest/python.py
@@ -251,21 +251,18 @@ class PyobjMixin(PyobjContext):
     @property
     def obj(self):
         """Underlying Python object."""
-        self._mount_obj_if_needed()
-        return self._obj
-
-    @obj.setter
-    def obj(self, value):
-        self._obj = value
-
-    def _mount_obj_if_needed(self):
         obj = getattr(self, "_obj", None)
         if obj is None:
             self._obj = obj = self._getobj()
             # XXX evil hack
             # used to avoid Instance collector marker duplication

diff --git a/testing/test_collection.py b/testing/test_collection.py
--- a/testing/test_collection.py
+++ b/testing/test_collection.py
@@ -1257,3 +1257,24 @@ def test_collector_respects_tbstyle(testdir):
             "*= 1 error in *",
         ]
     )
+
+
+def test_does_not_eagerly_collect_packages(testdir):
+    testdir.makepyfile("def test(): pass")
+    pydir = testdir.mkpydir("foopkg")
+    pydir.join("__init__.py").write("assert False")
+    result = testdir.runpytest()
+    assert result.ret == ExitCode.OK
+
+
+def test_does_not_put_src_on_path(testdir):
+    # `src` is not on sys.path so it should not be importable
+    testdir.tmpdir.join("src/nope/__init__.py").ensure()

parser.addini(
        "python_files",
        type="args",
        # NOTE: default is also used in AssertionRewritingHook.
        default=["test_*.py", "*_test.py"],
        help="glob-style file patterns for Python test module discovery",
    )

def test_collect_pyargs_with_testpaths(testdir, monkeypatch):
    testmod = testdir.mkdir("testmod")
    # NOTE: __init__.py is not collected since it does not match python_files.
    testmod.ensure("__init__.py").write("def test_func(): pass")
    testmod.ensure("test_file.py").write("def test_func(): pass")

    root = testdir.mkdir("root")
    root.ensure("pytest.ini").write(
        textwrap.dedent(
            """

def test_collectignore_via_conftest(testdir, monkeypatch):
    """collect_ignore in parent conftest skips importing child (issue #4592)."""
    tests = testdir.mkpydir("tests")
    tests.ensure("conftest.py").write("collect_ignore = ['ignore_me']")

    ignore_me = tests.mkdir("ignore_me")
    ignore_me.ensure("__init__.py")
    ignore_me.ensure("conftest.py").write("assert 0, 'should_not_be_called'")

    result = testdir.runpytest()
    assert result.ret == ExitCode.NO_TESTS_COLLECTED

pytest 5.2.3 (2019-11-14)
=========================

Bug Fixes
---------

- `#5830 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/5830>`_: The first test in a package (``__init__.py``) marked with ``@pytest.mark.skip`` is now correctly skipped.


- `#6099 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/6099>`_: Fix ``--trace`` when used with parametrized functions.

hindsight_observations.description: The regression was caused by package discovery creating Package collectors whose collect path eagerly mounted the underlying module object, thereby importing an encountered __init__.py even when it did not match python_files.
Eagerly importing a discovered package could also alter sys.path: traversing src/nope made nope importable even though src was not initially on the import path.

The hindsight tests establish two concrete regression manifestations: an unrelated package initializer that raises must not fail ordinary collection, and merely traversing a src-layout package must not make that package importable.

A pre-existing test for propagating a skip marker from a package __init__.py depended on importing that initializer during package collection and was removed when eager package importing was eliminated.
The selected regression suite passed after the change, including broader collection, ignore, package-init, and skipping coverage; this is validation evidence rather than an issue-time product choice.

implementation_incidentals.description: The gold implementation made PyobjMixin.obj itself perform lazy initialization and removed the separate _mount_obj_if_needed helper.
The gold implementation removed Module.__init__ and its __init__.py-specific _ALLOW_MARKERS override.
The gold implementation fixed the eager import by deleting the explicit object-mount call at the start of Package.collect; other lazy-import designs could satisfy the requested behavior.

The implementation used two specifically named regression tests in testing/test_collection.py and deleted test_skip_package from testing/test_skipping.py; those exact test organization choices are incidental.
